Here is the raw Python code to render frames 181 to 270 of the world map animation for a flight from Washington D.C. to New Delhi. It uses `matplotlib`, `cartopy`, and `pyproj` to calculate and draw the flight path accurately along a great circle and outputs the frames to a local `frames` directory.

```python
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import cartopy.crs as ccrs
import cartopy.feature as cfeature
import os
from pyproj import Geod

def generate_flight_frames(start_frame=181, end_frame=270, total_frames=360):
    # Coordinates for Washington D.C.
    lon1, lat1 = -77.0369, 38.9072
    # Coordinates for New Delhi
    lon2, lat2 = 77.2090, 28.6139

    # Calculate great circle points
    g = Geod(ellps='WGS84')
    # npts returns a list of intermediate points. We need total_frames - 2 intermediates.
    lonlats = g.npts(lon1, lat1, lon2, lat2, total_frames - 2)
    
    lons = [lon1] + [x[0] for x in lonlats] + [lon2]
    lats = [lat1] + [x[1] for x in lonlats] + [lat2]

    os.makedirs('frames', exist_ok=True)

    for i in range(start_frame - 1, end_frame):
        frame_num = i + 1
        
        fig = plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
        # Using the Robinson projection for a good global view
        ax = plt.axes(projection=ccrs.Robinson())
        ax.set_global()
        
        # Add map features
        ax.add_feature(cfeature.LAND, facecolor='lightgray')
        ax.add_feature(cfeature.OCEAN, facecolor='lightblue')
        ax.add_feature(cfeature.COASTLINE, linewidth=0.5)
        ax.add_feature(cfeature.BORDERS, linewidth=0.5, linestyle=':')
        
        # Plot the entire flight path in the background as dashed
        ax.plot(lons, lats, transform=ccrs.Geodetic(), color='gray', linestyle='--', alpha=0.5)
        
        # Plot the path traversed up to the current frame
        current_lons = lons[:frame_num]
        current_lats = lats[:frame_num]
        
        if len(current_lons) > 1:
            ax.plot(current_lons, current_lats, transform=ccrs.Geodetic(), color='red', linewidth=2)
            
        # Plot the current position of the plane/dot
        ax.plot(current_lons[-1], current_lats[-1], transform=ccrs.Geodetic(), marker='o', color='blue', markersize=6)
        
        # Highlight start and destination cities
        ax.plot(lon1, lat1, transform=ccrs.Geodetic(), marker='*', color='green', markersize=10, label="Washington D.C.")
        ax.plot(lon2, lat2, transform=ccrs.Geodetic(), marker='*', color='purple', markersize=10, label="New Delhi")
        
        plt.title(f"Flight from Washington D.C. to New Delhi - Frame {frame_num:03d}")
        plt.legend(loc='lower left')
        
        # Save frame to disk
        out_path = f"frames/frame_{frame_num:03d}.png"
        plt.savefig(out_path, dpi=150, bbox_inches='tight')
        plt.close(fig)
        
        print(f"Rendered frame {frame_num} / {total_frames}")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Render the requested batch: frames 181 to 270 (out of 360)
    generate_flight_frames(start_frame=181, end_frame=270, total_frames=360)
```
